notes: Patch is byte-identical to the vulnerable function; explanation falsely claims it is already correct, so CWE-428 is untouched.
Only swaps dlopen(path) for dlopen(ret->path), which is the same string; no CWE-428 mitigation and the TOCTOU rationale is wrong.
Adds an absolute-path requirement and RTLD_LOCAL, blocking relative-path hijacking but not verifying the provider is a FIDO library; rejects formerly valid relative paths.
Unchanged function; explanation describes a bounds check that is not present in the patch.
Adds minimum-header and negative-length checks and verifies each extended bitmap word fits before reading; correct OOB-read fix.
Unchanged function; explanation claims a fix that the patch does not contain, leaving the double-free/UAF path intact.
Frees the placeholder at every switch branch while refs still points at it, then frees it again via ref_idx->data: introduces a double-free/UAF instead of fixing the root cause.
Same repeated free_object(ret) pattern as the other candidate; placeholder remains referenced in refs and is freed again later, a new double-free path.
Computes strlen separately and casts to u32, but leaves the 51/1 size constants that upstream corrects, so the box-size defect remains; the narrowing cast can itself truncate.
Adds a SIZE_MAX overflow check and then truncates the length to u32; does not fix the size-constant miscalculation and introduces a new GF_ISOM_INVALID_FILE return path.
Function text is unchanged; the explanation claims a props initialization that does not exist in the patch, and the what==3 mishandling remains.
Adds a depth bounds guard unrelated to CWE-200; the fallback branch still treats what==3 values as section_type, so private sections are still exposed.
Identical depth-guard change; no handling for what==3/setPrivate, so the information-exposure root cause is untouched.
Adds a bin==NULL guard but leaves the signed int len parameter that upstream changes to size_t, so the CWE-190 root cause is untouched.
Unchanged function; explanation asserts no defect, contradicting the annotated integer-overflow issue.
Same unrelated NULL check as the other candidate; length type remains int and the integer issue is not addressed.
No-op patch (byte-identical to the vulnerable wrapper); explanation denies any defect, so CWE-200 is unaddressed.
Only reindented; still delegates with NULL blinding parameters and the explanation claims no defect.
Same unchanged wrapper with cosmetic indentation; no mitigation for the missing deterministic-signing blinding.
Adds st != NULL before dereferencing st->state, which is the unchecked-allocation NULL-dereference root cause; surrounding behavior is preserved, with only formatting tidies.
Same st != NULL guard in the fencing branch; no other semantic change, so callers see the same behavior apart from the avoided crash.
Identical NULL guard and formatting cleanup; correctly prevents dereferencing a failed stonith_api_new() result.
Bounds the unbounded %s conversions to the actual buffer sizes (%9s device, %4095s file), directly fixing the stack overflow with no other logic change.
Bounds both %s fields and also adds a strlcat return-value early-out, which introduces a new truncation failure path beyond the overflow fix.
Same bounded conversions plus the extra strlcat truncation check; overflow is fixed but an additional control-flow exit is added.
Replaces a NULL salt with an empty string and guards a NULL crypt result, avoiding the crash but still permitting the weak empty-salt hash; upstream instead asserts non-NULL salt.
Rejects NULL or empty salt and checks the crypt result, removing the NULL dereference; however empty salt now returns an empty String instead of a hash, a caller-visible behavior change.
Rejects NULL/empty salt before calling crypt, eliminating the dereference, but also changes the documented empty-salt behavior and omits the crypt result check.
Changes zsocket_set_sndbuf to zsocket_set_rcvbuf for rcvBuf, an unrelated config bug; the CWE-134 format-string sink zsocket_bind(description) is untouched.
Same unrelated rcvBuf setter fix plus a zctx_new NULL check; the uncontrolled format string passed to zsocket_bind/connect is still present.
Fixes the rcvBuf setter and adds a context NULL check, neither of which addresses the CWE-134 format-string vulnerability in the bind/connect calls.
Patch is byte-identical to the vulnerable function; keeping ASSERT(header->checkHeader()) means the header validation still disappears in release builds.
Replaces the unchecked advance with a bounded while loop that rejects zero or oversized headers relative to payloadEnd, a valid alternative fix for the out-of-bounds read.
Adds only a size==0 guard; decoded bytes are still written unsanitized, so CR/LF header injection through %0d%0a remains.
Same size==0 guard with no filtering of decoded control characters; the CWE-113/116 root cause is untouched.
Adds the size guard and validates hex digits, but valid %0d%0a still decodes to CRLF and is stored, so header injection is not mitigated.
Fixes the missing strchr NULL check and the one-byte terminator overflow in the [ branch, but leaves recursion unbounded, so CWE-674 stack exhaustion is untouched.
Same NULL/off-by-one corrections to the format-specifier branch; no recursion depth limit, so the annotated uncontrolled-recursion defect remains.
Adds the strchr NULL check and requires p-fmt < sizeof(s), fixing a different overflow, but never caps smb_fdata recursion depth.
Patch is identical to the vulnerable inclusive-bound comparison; the explanation denies any defect, so the off-by-one frame boundary remains.
Unchanged inclusive comparison of frameRight/frameBottom; explanation claims no security defect despite the annotated access-control boundary error.
No-op patch; the <= boundaries that upstream changes to < are preserved, so the boundary miscalculation is not fixed.
Replaces pointer-addition overflow check with cbStatsMsgIn > remaining bytes and casts the sizeof comparison; the stats-blob bounds check is now overflow-safe.
Same subtraction-based stats-size check matching the upstream repair; no other semantic change.
Adds the (int)sizeof cast and the non-overflowing remaining-bytes comparison; correctly fixes the oversized-stats path.
Function is unchanged; the explanation claims a 255-byte scan bound that the patch does not add, so the NULL password dereference remains.
Adds a NULL check and rewrites the scan as a bounded 0..254 loop plus terminator check, fixing the out-of-bounds read while preserving dummy-password detection.
Adds a NULL check after createDummyConnection, a null-dereference hardening; the 65535-byte dummy allocation that upstream replaces with sendBufferSize (CWE-770) is unchanged.
Same NULL guard only; the hard-coded 65535 buffer size remains, so the resource-consumption root cause is not addressed.
Adds the NULL guard and also changes the implicit-int return type to void, a signature change; the oversized dummy allocation is untouched.
Unchanged function; the explanation describes overflow guards that are not present, and the 32-bit width*channels overflow remains.
Casts the row-factor multiplication to png_alloc_size_t and adds explicit overflow checks before multiplication, addition and division, matching the upstream fix intent.
Same alloc-size casts with overflow checks plus a row_factor==0 guard; the IDAT limit computation no longer wraps and stays clamped to PNG_UINT_31_MAX.
Adds only a (void) cast on touch_file; the mode argument that upstream changes to MODE_INVALID (CWE-264) is untouched, so no access-control defect is fixed.
Same no-op (void) cast, leaving the insecure touch_file mode and the rest of the function unchanged.
Explicitly discards the touch_file return value but keeps the 0 mode argument; the access-control root cause is not addressed.
Function is byte-identical to the vulnerable version; the missing read-only shadow-table check remains and the explanation denies any defect.

Only adds an empty-string fallback when both column text and nullvalue are NULL; the nbuf[200] number buffer that upstream enlarges to JSI_MAX_NUMBER_STRING is unchanged.
Same NULL-text fallback, unrelated to the CWE-120 buffer-size issue; no change to nbuf sizing or Jsi_NumberToString usage.
Patch is byte-identical to the vulnerable function; the explanation claims the narrowing conversions are already safe, so the CWE-20 validation gap remains.

Adds negative and overflow guards to the accumulators; the bool-to-DataReductionRequestType signature/type correction that upstream makes is not addressed.

Replaces DCHECKs with runtime negative/overflow returns, but the CWE-416-relevant parameter type change (bool to DataReductionRequestType) is missing.
Function is unchanged; the sanitize_string calls on name/var that upstream adds are absent, and the explanation asserts no defect.

No-op patch with an explanation denying any defect; no sanitization of the metadata key or value.
